title: Choosing an approach: team, performance, device features and time

videos.script:
Ask which approach is best, and you will get an argument. {{argument}} Ask which is best for this team, this app and this deadline, and you can get an answer.

This lesson turns the choice into criteria. {{criteria}} The languages the team already knows. The device features the app needs, and how new they are. How smooth it has to be. How soon it has to ship, on how many platforms. And what it costs to keep for years. Notice that none of these is a fact about a tool. Each one is a fact about the team, the app or the calendar.

You will watch three made-up teams decide, and each lands somewhere different. {{teams}} Then you run a small scoring program for the planner, and change one weight. {{flip}} The ranking flips. That is the lesson's real point: the weights are the decision, so write them down where people can argue with them.

Last, you meet the track's fork, which asks you this same question. {{fork}}
